MAX-A-MILLION's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The second-biggest prize left on "MAX-A-MILLION" is $100,000, with six of them remaining.

Everything above about "MAX-A-MILLION" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
985.headline: Same price, different prizes

988.body:
The most common win left on "Emerald 10's" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Tomorrow's count on "Emerald 10's" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
988.headline: What's actually left to win

990.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "LADY LUCK" have been sold. The game is well into its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "LADY LUCK" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
990.headline: Tickets sold so far

992.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$2 MILLION VAULT" are sold. The top prize count has held, with one of three still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "$2 MILLION VAULT" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
992.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for four months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "$5,000 Triple Play", with every prize level included.
993.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

994.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$25,000 Triple Play", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with one of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything above about "$25,000 Triple Play" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
994.headline: How much has sold

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has had no $200,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "$200,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 21.
995.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

996.body:
$1,000,000 Triple Play's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about three-quarters is in wins under $1,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

If "$1,000,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
